picks.rationale: New free open-source tool (Agent-Native Plans) for reviewing an agent's plan and output. Design-to-code teams can use it the next day.
picks.excerpt: Builder.io introduces Agent-Native Plans, a free open-source tool for reviewing what a coding agent plans to build and what it built, so teams agree on intent up front instead of watching tool calls.

picks.rationale: The new angle is COMSOL Multiphysics 2027's MCP server, which lets AI agents drive simulation models. Frame the card on COMSOL MCP, not the SimScale/Onshape agent already covered 09-17.
picks.excerpt: COMSOL previewed Multiphysics 2027 with an MCP server so AI agents can drive simulation models, Onshape users can now run SimScale simulations via an AI agent, plus Autodesk corrections on neural CAD's status after AU 2026.

picks.rationale: West Monroe's chief people officer argues AI transformation is really owned by 'builders' close to the work who redesign their own workflows, and that orgs should measure outcomes, not AI usage counts. A practical frame for design leaders running AX.
picks.excerpt: Argues AI transformation is owned less by the chief AI officer than by 'builders' close to the work who redesign their own workflows, and that orgs should measure how people rethink work with AI rather than usage counts.

picks.rationale: Covers a design-system pain point: AI-generated React still has to be remapped to existing components and tokens. Proposes generating directly inside the UI kit instead.
picks.excerpt: AI builds screens fast, but exported React still has to be remapped to the existing design system's components and tokens; the post proposes generating directly inside the UI kit so there is no handoff.

picks.rationale: Uses Figma hiring data (56% of hiring managers want more seniors vs 25% hiring juniors) to argue design leaders must grow junior judgment now that AI does starter work. A practice and career insight.
picks.excerpt: Citing Figma data that 56% of hiring managers want more senior designers vs 25% hiring juniors, Patrick Neeman argues AI tools have absorbed starter work and design leaders must deliberately grow junior judgment.
